historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (FY2022-FY2025), cross-checked against FY2026 guidance: ~2.5% systemwide-sales contribution from net unit growth plus H1-2026 comps of +2.5% = mid-single-digit systemwide sales; H1-2026 revenue +6.4% reported with an FX tailwind. Equity CAGR is unusable (deficit).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity has been a deficit since FY2016 (debt-funded buybacks), so the equity CAGR is undefined and cannot be the anchor. EPS CAGRs (12.7% 3yr / 13.6% 5yr) exceed revenue CAGRs (5.1% / 7.0%) by far more than 30%: the 5yr window starts at the FY2020 COVID trough and both windows carry margin expansion (operating margin 40.4% FY2022 -> 46.1% FY2025) plus ~1%/yr buyback shrinkage. Neither EPS CAGR is a forward revenue assumption.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (reported FCF less SBC) CAGRs 9.7% / 9.2% vs reported 9.4% / 9.2%: SBC is ~0.6% of revenue and growing in line with cash flow, so the SBC adjustment does not change the growth picture. FCF CAGRs are flattered by the FY2020 base (5yr) and the FY2022 working-capital-depressed year (3yr); revenue is the honest anchor for a mature franchisor.

scenario_narratives.base: McDonald's remains a ~95%-franchised rent-plus-royalty annuity growing with the unit base. Net unit growth contributes ~2.5%/yr to systemwide sales through the 50,000-restaurant target in 2028, U.S. comps stay low-single-digit (value platform compliance improves from the acknowledged 60-65% but lower-income traffic stays soft) while IOM/IDL run a point or two faster, and reported revenue grows 5.5% in FY2026 decelerating to 3% by the end of the decade. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin holds ~55-55.5%: franchised-margin growth offsets company-operated cost inflation. Capex stays at the guided 3.7-3.9B (13.4% of revenue) while the unit push runs, then normalises toward 10.5%. Cash tax 22%. Owner FCF margin builds from ~31% to ~34% of revenue as capex intensity eases; a 20x cap binds against Gordon at 7.5%/2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The MCD NEXT value reset actually lands: the system standardises the under-$3 / $5 platform, loyalty hits 250M 90-day actives and $45B of loyalty sales by 2027, and U.S. traffic turns positive while Japan, UK, Germany and Australia keep compounding, so systemwide sales run high-single-digit and revenue grows 6.5% for two years before decelerating to 3.5%. Franchised mix and G&A at 2.2% of systemwide sales lift the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 57% by FY2031. Unit growth keeps capex at 12-13% of revenue a year longer, then 10.5%. Terminal growth 3% with a 22x cap, reflecting the quality of a real-estate-backed royalty stream.
scenario_narratives.bear: The lower-income U.S. consumer stays squeezed and the value war with Wendy's, Burger King and Taco Bell becomes structural: franchisees resist mandated value pricing, so McDonald's funds it through rent/royalty relief and higher company-operated subsidies. U.S. comps hover around zero, FX turns from tailwind to headwind, and revenue growth is 3.5% in FY2026 then 2-2.5% - essentially unit growth alone. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin slips to 53% as company-operated margins keep eroding (-6% in Q2-2026) and beef/labour inflation is only partly passed through. Capex guidance is honoured near term (the unit pipeline is committed) then cut as returns on new units disappoint. Cash tax 23%. Terminal growth 2% with a 17x cap: still a durable business, but one the market reprices as ex-growth with 3.6x net debt/EBITDA and negative book equity. No zero-floor risk - owner FCF stays strongly positive throughout.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A franchised real-estate royalty annuity valued as the unlevered owner-FCF it throws off, with the 39B of net debt deducted once in the bridge. Margins are built from components (pre-SBC EBITDA, SBC, D&A, 22% cash tax, guided capex) rather than carried forward, and the horizon is 10 years so the elevated unit-growth capex has time to normalise before the terminal year is capitalised. The flat share count ignores the ~1%/yr buyback shrinkage, which is deliberate: buybacks are value-neutral in the owner-FCF frame. Terminal value is capped at 17-22x year-10 FCF and dominates the result, so the finding is a value range around the current price rather than a precise number.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is roughly two-thirds of enterprise value; each 1pp of WACC moves the base case by tens of dollars per share (see sensitivity grid)
Capex intensity: if the 50,000-unit push does not roll off toward 10.5% of revenue after 2028, owner FCF margin stalls ~3pp below the modelled terminal level
U.S. value-platform execution and lower-income traffic - the Q2-2026 miss was two-thirds attributed to inconsistent franchisee implementation
Company-operated margin erosion from beef, packaging and labour inflation (California-style wage laws), only ~36% of revenue but the part McDonald's bears directly
FX: ~70% of revenue is non-U.S.; H1-2026 growth carried a dollar tailwind that reverses if the dollar strengthens

Leverage: 3.6x net debt/EBITDA with negative book equity - refinancing at higher rates (interest guided +4-6% in 2026) is charged through the bridge, not the flows, so a rising net debt figure flows straight to equity value
Joint-employer / franchise-model litigation and regulation that could shift labour liability onto the franchisor

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 229.61-341.75
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 63908) via MCD_Metrics.csv / MCD.duckdb through Q2-2026; Q2-2026 10-Q (mcd-20260630.htm) balance sheet, EPS note, nonoperating table and Outlook section read directly for net debt, diluted shares, interest income and FY2026 guidance
data_sources.qualitative: MCD_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): business model, bull/bear axes, Q2-2026 results and guidance commentary

inputs.share_count_basis: 707.6M shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, 2026-06-30) plus 2.0M treasury-method dilutive share-based awards from the 10-Q EPS note = 709.6M fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Q2-2026 diluted weighted average was 711.1M.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement add-back (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation 165M). MCD publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-award-tax figure and does not tag net-share-settlement withholding separately; at 0.6% of revenue the omission is immaterial.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases 2,056M (H1-2026: 1,251M) against dividends of 5,115M. The flat count is funded: buybacks run at ~12x the SBC charge, so the share count actually declines ~1%/yr, which the model does not credit (it is value-neutral in the owner-FCF frame).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 229.61-341.75, price sits at the bottom of the range
inputs.net_debt_note: Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet: long-term debt 39,863 (includes ~2.35B of finance lease liabilities, per the FY2025 10-K lease note) less cash 822 = 39,041. No short-term borrowings / current maturities line on the June-2026 balance sheet (total current liabilities 4,018 reconciles without one). Operating lease liabilities (690 current + 14,039 non-current) are NOT in net debt - see lease_treatment.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Rf ~4.1% (10y UST), beta ~0.75, ERP 5.2% -> cost of equity ~8.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.3% (FY2025 interest 1,582M on ~39.5B average debt = 4.0%, new issuance higher; 2026 interest guided +4-6%), after-tax ~3.4%; market-value weights ~81% equity / 19% debt at the current (52-week-low) price -> ~7.1%. Rounded up to 7.5% because the equity weight is being measured at a depressed price and the business carries 3.6x net debt/EBITDA with negative book equity. Same WACC in all three scenarios - risk is charged once, through the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842. Operating leases: rent expense (~1.6B/yr, mostly the land/building leases MCD sub-leases to franchisees) stays inside operating expenses, so EBITDA is post-rent and the 14.7B operating lease liability is excluded from net debt. Finance leases (~2.35B): the liability sits inside the reported long-term debt line and is therefore in net debt, while their amortisation (in D&A) and interest (in interest expense) are below EBITDA. Each lease class charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None - no non-controlling interests. Equity-method affiliates (investments in affiliates 2,896M at 2026-06-30: McDonald's Japan ~35%, China JV ~48%, etc.) are NOT added in the equity bridge because 'equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates' is a line inside operating income and so already inside the EBITDA being capitalised (matching-asset rule: income kept, asset not added).
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income was 37M in FY2025 and 19M in H1-2026 on a <1B cash balance against 39B of net debt; nothing to strip. The engine is unlevered (EBITDA -> NOPAT) and deducts net debt, so the 1.58B interest expense is charged through the bridge, not the flows.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: operating company - franchised QSR with a real-estate rent annuity; not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco/distressed shell). First valuation of this ticker, no MEMORY.md entry. US filer, USD throughout, no NCI, no dual currency, no SBC-zero issue, so owner-fcf-adaptations.md was not needed beyond the lease rule applied above. EBITDA driver is PRE-SBC adjusted EBITDA (operating income + D&A + SBC: FY2025 12,393 + 2,199 + 165 = 14,757 = 54.9% of revenue; H1-2026 55.2%), and SBC is then deducted on its own line; the CSV's EBITDA column (14,592) is post-SBC. FY0 revenue 26,885 (FY2025). Component year-1 sanity: revenue 28.4B x 55.0% EBITDA - 0.6% SBC - 8.2% D&A = EBIT ~46.2% (guidance: operating margin mid-to-high 40s) x (1-22%) + D&A - 13.4% capex = unlevered owner FCF ~8.7B; less ~1.3B after-tax interest = ~7.4B levered, which ties to management's FY2026 FCF-conversion guidance (low-to-mid 80% of ~8.9B net income = 7.1-7.6B). Horizon 10 years because capex is guided elevated (3.7-3.9B in 2026, majority for new units toward 50,000 restaurants by 2028) and the FCF margin only normalises once unit growth decelerates; terminal-year capex 10.5% vs D&A 8.0% leaves 2.5% of revenue of net reinvestment to fund 2.5% terminal growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +5.5%: H1 +6.4% reported with an FX tailwind, Q2 global comps only +1.3% (U.S. +0.8%) with IOM/IDL guided to accelerate sequentially; unit growth ~2.5% is the floor. Decelerates to 3% by FY2034-35 as unit growth slows past the 50,000-restaurant target and comps revert to low-single-digit pricing plus modest traffic.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA margin 54.9% FY2025, 55.2% H1-2026; guidance operating margin mid-to-high 40s. Franchised-margin growth (+4.3% in Q2) offsets company-operated margin erosion (-6% in Q2); 50bp of mix/G&A leverage over four years, then flat.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guided 3.7-3.9B (13.4% of ~28.4B revenue), majority for ~750 company/IOM-market openings a year toward 50,000 global units by 2028; FY2025 actual 12.5%, FY2024 10.7%, FY2019-23 average ~9.5%. Elevated through the 2028 target, then eases to 10.5%, still above the pre-2024 norm because new-unit economics now carry more of the growth than refranchising.
base.cash_tax_rationale: FY2026 ETR guided 21-23%; FY2025 cash taxes paid 2,688M = 21.7% of EBIT. No NOLs, credits or valuation-allowance effects to ramp.
base.wc_rationale: Working capital changes were -215M (H1-2026), -620M (H1-2025) and roughly zero over FY2023-25: a franchisor collects rent and royalties monthly with minimal inventory, so growth neither consumes nor releases meaningful cash. Set to zero.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 20/50/30. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs three independent things to go right at once - U.S. value-platform compliance that management has publicly conceded is only 60-65%, a U.S. traffic turn among lower-income consumers, and sustained international acceleration - and the stock sitting at a 52-week low says the market is not underwriting them. Bear lifted to 20% because the Q2-2026 U.S. comp miss (+0.8%) and declining company-operated margins are already visible, not hypothetical; it stays well short of 25-35% because there is no going-concern, covenant or single-customer risk - the franchised rent/royalty stream covers interest ~8x. Base 50%: a mature compounder growing roughly with its unit base is the central case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
sanity_check.not_evaluated_reason: no rule had inputs: no annual row with revenue, equity or earnings on a known scale (core_metrics.units NULL? see make backfill-units) or no FY-end price aligned to it
